question: In 2017, who became the first Indian singer to make it to Delhi's Madame Tussauds Museum?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shreya Ghoshal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 2017, the renowned playback singer Shreya Ghoshal became the first Indian singer to have her wax statue installed at Delhi's Madame Tussauds Museum. (श्रेया घोषाल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Shreya Ghoshal is a multiple National Film Award-winning singer, known for songs in Hindi and many regional languages.

• Madame Tussauds is a famous wax museum (originally in London) with branches worldwide, displaying wax figures of celebrities.

NOTE

• Indian personalities with wax statues at Madame Tussauds include Mahatma Gandhi, Sachin Tendulkar, Amitabh Bachchan, Narendra Modi and A. R. Rahman.

question: Vitamin D is synthesised using sunshine, by the:
solution_text:
The correct answer is skin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vitamin D is synthesised in the skin when it is exposed to sunlight (ultraviolet-B rays). The UV rays convert a cholesterol derivative in the skin into Vitamin D. (त्वचा — विटामिन D का संश्लेषण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and phosphorus, keeping bones and teeth strong.

• Its deficiency causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

NOTE

• Vitamin D is called the "sunshine vitamin". Other sources include fish, egg yolk and fortified milk. Fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, K.

question: In which weight category did Nitu Ghanghas win the IBA Women's World Boxing Championship event, 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 48 kg.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nitu Ghanghas won the gold medal in the 48 kg (minimumweight) category at the IBA Women's World Boxing Championships 2023, held in New Delhi. (नीतू घनघस — 48 किग्रा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• At the same 2023 championship, Nikhat Zareen, Lovlina Borgohain and Saweety Boora also won gold medals for India.

• Boxing is governed internationally by the International Boxing Association (IBA).

NOTE

• India's boxing icons: Mary Kom (six-time World Champion), Nikhat Zareen (World Champion) and Lovlina Borgohain (Olympic medallist).

question: As on 31st October 2023, the youngest member of parliament (in terms of age) in the 17th Lok Sabha, Chandrani Murmu, represents which political party?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Biju Janata Dal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chandrani Murmu, the youngest Member of Parliament in the 17th Lok Sabha, represents the Biju Janata Dal (BJD) from the Keonjhar constituency of Odisha. (चंद्राणी मुर्मू — बीजू जनता दल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• She was elected in 2019 at the age of about 25 years, becoming the youngest MP in that Lok Sabha.

• The minimum age to become a member of the Lok Sabha is 25 years (Article 84).

NOTE

• The Biju Janata Dal (BJD) is a regional party of Odisha, founded by Naveen Patnaik in 1997, named after his father Biju Patnaik.

question: The institution like Lokpal or Lokayukta (Ombudsman) was first created in which of the following countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sweden.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The institution of the "Ombudsman" (like the Lokpal/Lokayukta in India) was first created in Sweden (in 1809). An Ombudsman is an official appointed to investigate complaints of maladministration and corruption. (स्वीडन — ओम्बड्समैन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• In India, the Lokpal (at the Centre) and Lokayuktas (in the states) are anti-corruption ombudsman institutions.

• The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act was passed in 2013; India's first Lokpal was Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose (2019).

NOTE

• The Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC), 1966, first recommended setting up the Lokpal and Lokayukta in India.

question: Which of the following structures has the IUPAC name 7-hydroxy-5-methylheptan-2-one?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Structure B.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The IUPAC name "7-hydroxy-5-methylheptan-2-one" describes a 7-carbon chain (heptan) with:

◦ a ketone group (=O) at carbon 2 ("-2-one"),

◦ a hydroxyl group (–OH) at carbon 7 ("7-hydroxy"),

◦ a methyl branch (–CH₃) at carbon 5 ("5-methyl").

• Structure B is the one that correctly shows all these features in the right positions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• In IUPAC nomenclature, the principal functional group (here, the ketone) gets the lowest possible number, and substituents (hydroxy, methyl) are named as prefixes with their locant numbers.

NOTE

• Common functional-group suffixes: -ol (alcohol), -one (ketone), -al (aldehyde), -oic acid (carboxylic acid). Here "-one" (ketone) is the main group and "hydroxy-" is a prefix.

question: What is the title of Sania Mirza's autobiography?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ace Against Odds.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ace Against Odds" is the autobiography of the ace Indian tennis player Sania Mirza. (सानिया मिर्ज़ा की आत्मकथा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Sania Mirza was a World No. 1 in women's doubles and won six Grand Slam titles (in doubles and mixed doubles). She received the Padma Bhushan and Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna.

• The word "ace" in tennis means a serve the opponent cannot touch.

NOTE

• Autobiographies: Changing India (Manmohan Singh), Wings of Fire (A. P. J. Abdul Kalam), The Test of My Life (Yuvraj Singh).

question: Which of the following was the capital of Vatsa Mahajanapada?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kausambi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kausambi" (near present-day Prayagraj/Allahabad, Uttar Pradesh) was the capital of the Vatsa Mahajanapada. (वत्स महाजनपद की राजधानी — कौशांबी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Some Mahajanapadas and their capitals: Magadha – Rajgir/Pataliputra; Kosala – Shravasti; Vatsa – Kausambi; Avanti – Ujjain/Mahishmati; Panchala – Ahichchatra; Vajji – Vaishali.

• The 16 Mahajanapadas existed around the 6th century BCE; Magadha eventually became the most powerful.

NOTE

• The Vatsa Mahajanapada's famous ruler was Udayana. Kausambi was an important centre of trade and Buddhism.

question: Where was the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association established in the year 1928?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)" was established in 1928 at the Feroz Shah Kotla ground in Delhi. (हिंदुस्तान सोशलिस्ट रिपब्लिकन एसोसिएशन — दिल्ली, 1928)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The HSRA was formed by reorganising the earlier Hindustan Republican Association (HRA), under the leadership of Chandra Shekhar Azad, with members like Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru and Bhagwati Charan Vohra.

• It aimed at achieving independence through revolutionary means and establishing a socialist republic.

NOTE

• The HRA (1924) was founded at Kanpur by Ram Prasad Bismil, Sachindra Nath Sanyal and others; it was linked to the Kakori Conspiracy (1925).

question: In June 2023, which state government among the following has announced the 'Shakti' scheme for free bus travel for women and trans people within the state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In June 2023, the Karnataka government announced the "Shakti" scheme, providing free bus travel for women and transgender persons within the state. (शक्ति योजना — कर्नाटक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Under the scheme, women and trans people can travel free in government (non-luxury) buses across Karnataka.

• "Shakti" was one of the five poll guarantees of the Karnataka government aimed at women's empowerment and mobility.

NOTE

• Similar welfare schemes exist in other states (e.g., free bus travel for women in Delhi and Tamil Nadu), aimed at improving women's access to transport and employment.

question: According to Article _____, no religious instruction shall be provided in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 28.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 28 of the Constitution provides that no religious instruction shall be provided in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds. It deals with freedom from attending religious instruction in certain educational institutions. (अनुच्छेद 28)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 25 — freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion.

• Article 26 — freedom to manage religious affairs.

• Article 27 — freedom from taxes for promotion of any particular religion.

• Articles 25–28 together form the Right to Freedom of Religion.

NOTE

• Article 29 (protection of minorities' language/culture) and Article 30 (right of minorities to establish educational institutions) form the Cultural and Educational Rights.

question: Which structure within the nucleus contains genetic information in the form of DNA?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chromosome.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Chromosomes" are the structures within the nucleus that carry the genetic information in the form of DNA. (गुणसूत्र — डीएनए)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A chromosome is made of DNA and proteins (histones); a segment of DNA that codes for a trait is a gene.

• Humans have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs) in each body cell.

NOTE

• Ribosomes make proteins; the nucleolus makes ribosomes; vacuoles store substances. Only chromosomes carry the hereditary (genetic) information.

question: Which of the following is the first planned industrial city in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jamshedpur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Jamshedpur" (in Jharkhand) is regarded as the first planned industrial city in India. It was founded by Jamsetji Nusserwanji Tata and grew around the Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO), established in 1907. (जमशेदपुर — पहला नियोजित औद्योगिक शहर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Jamshedpur is also called "Tatanagar" or the "Steel City".

• Chandigarh was India's first planned modern city (designed by the architect Le Corbusier), but Jamshedpur is specifically the first planned industrial city.

NOTE

• Jamshedpur is one of the few cities in India managed by a company (Tata Steel) rather than a municipal corporation, and is known for its greenery and planning.

question: Which of the following is NOT a commercial bank?
option_2: The Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India Bank
option_4: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development)" is NOT a commercial bank — it is an apex development/refinance institution for agriculture and rural development. (नाबार्ड — विकास बैंक, वाणिज्यिक बैंक नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• SBI, ICICI Bank and the Development Bank of Singapore (DBS) are all commercial banks (they accept deposits and give loans for profit).

• NABARD (established 1982) provides refinance to rural financial institutions and promotes rural development (it does not deal directly with the public like a commercial bank).

NOTE

• Apex/specialised institutions: RBI (central bank), NABARD (rural/agriculture), SIDBI (small industries), EXIM Bank (export–import).

question: Who among the following received the Nritya Kalanidhi for the year 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bragha Bessell.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bragha Bessell, a renowned Bharatanatyam exponent, received the "Nritya Kalanidhi" award for the year 2022, conferred by the Music Academy, Chennai. (नृत्य कलानिधि — ब्रागा बेसेल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Nritya Kalanidhi is a prestigious award given by the Music Academy, Madras (Chennai) for excellence in classical dance.

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance form of Tamil Nadu, renowned for its expressive abhinaya.

NOTE

• The Music Academy, Chennai, also confers the "Sangita Kalanidhi" award, one of the highest honours in Carnatic music.

question: Bhamidipati Srivalli Rashmika is associated with which game?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lawn Tennis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bhamidipati Srivalli Rashmika is an Indian sportsperson associated with the game of Lawn Tennis. (लॉन टेनिस)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Lawn Tennis is played on a rectangular court with a net in the middle; the four Grand Slam tournaments are the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and US Open.

• India's notable tennis players include Leander Paes, Mahesh Bhupathi and Sania Mirza.

NOTE

• Scoring terms in tennis: love (0), 15, 30, 40, deuce (40-40), advantage, ace, fault.

question: In which of the following years was a Hindu College in Benaras established to impart education from the ancient Sanskrit texts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1791.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A Sanskrit College (Hindu College) at Benaras (Varanasi) was established in 1791 by Jonathan Duncan, the British Resident, to promote the study of ancient Sanskrit texts and Hindu law. (बनारस संस्कृत कॉलेज — 1791)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Earlier, the Calcutta Madrasa was set up by Warren Hastings in 1781 to promote the study of Muslim/Arabic and Persian law.

• These institutions reflected the early Orientalist policy of promoting traditional Indian learning.

NOTE

• The Asiatic Society of Bengal was founded by Sir William Jones in 1784 to study Indian languages, history and culture.

question: Which festival is celebrated at Sabarimala temple, on the occassion of Makar Sakranti?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Makaravilakku.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Makaravilakku" is the festival celebrated at the Sabarimala temple (Kerala) on the occasion of Makar Sankranti (mid-January). It is associated with the sighting of the "Makara Jyoti" (a celestial light/star). (मकरविलक्कु — सबरीमाला)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Sabarimala temple is dedicated to Lord Ayyappa and is one of the most famous pilgrimage sites in South India.

• Makaravilakku draws millions of devotees who undertake a strict 41-day penance before the pilgrimage.

NOTE

• Festivals of Kerala: Onam (harvest festival), Vishu (New Year), Thrissur Pooram and Makaravilakku (at Sabarimala).

question: Former Indian actress Vyjayanthimala was trained in which classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The veteran Indian actress Vyjayanthimala was trained in the Bharatanatyam classical dance form. She was one of the earliest actresses to be a trained classical dancer. (भरतनाट्यम — वैजयंतीमाला)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharat Muni.

• Vyjayanthimala was a leading actress of Hindi and Tamil cinema and was later honoured with the Padma Shri and elected to Parliament.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

question: Who among the following was the first sultan of Delhi Sultanate to visit the Ajmer shrine of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate to visit the Ajmer shrine (dargah) of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti. (मुहम्मद बिन तुगलक — अजमेर दरगाह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti (also called Gharib Nawaz) was the founder of the Chishti Sufi order in India; his dargah at Ajmer is a major pilgrimage centre.

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq (r. 1325–1351) is known for his ambitious but failed experiments — the transfer of the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad and the introduction of token (bronze) currency.

NOTE

• The Chishti order was the most popular Sufi silsila in India, preaching love, tolerance and devotion. Later, Emperor Akbar was also a great devotee of the Ajmer shrine.

question: In which year was Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (Scheme) announced by the Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2014.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)" was launched/announced by the Government of India in 2014. It is a skill development and placement programme for rural youth. (डीडीयू-जीकेवाई — 2014)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• DDU-GKY is part of the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) under the Ministry of Rural Development.

• It aims to provide skill training to poor rural youth (aged 15–35) and place them in wage employment.

NOTE

• It was launched on 25 September 2014, the birth anniversary of Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya, to help realise the "demographic dividend" of rural India.

question: In Kerala and coastal area of Karnataka the pre-monsoon shower is known as _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mango shower.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Kerala and the coastal areas of Karnataka, the pre-monsoon showers (in April–May) are known as "Mango showers" because they help in the early ripening of mangoes. (आम्र वर्षा / मैंगो शावर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• In Karnataka, these pre-monsoon showers are also called "Cherry blossoms/Blossom showers" as they help the coffee flowers to bloom.

• In West Bengal and Assam, violent pre-monsoon thunderstorms are called "Kalbaisakhi (Nor'westers)"; in Assam, "Bardoichila".

NOTE

• Pre-monsoon showers bring relief from summer heat and benefit crops like mangoes, coffee and tea.

question: According to the Human Development Index 2023-24, what is the rank of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 134.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Human Development Index (HDI) 2023-24 (released by the UNDP), India was ranked 134 out of the countries assessed. (मानव विकास सूचकांक 2023-24 — भारत का रैंक 134)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The HDI measures development using three dimensions — health (life expectancy), education (years of schooling) and standard of living (GNI per capita).

• It was developed by economists Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen and is published in the Human Development Report.

NOTE

• HDI values range from 0 to 1: very high (0.8+), high, medium and low human development. India is in the medium human development category.

question: Plutonic rocks are formed when lava cools _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is in the crust.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Plutonic (intrusive igneous) rocks" are formed when magma cools and solidifies slowly deep beneath the Earth's surface, i.e., within the crust. The slow cooling gives them large, coarse crystals (e.g., granite). (प्लूटोनिक चट्टानें — भूपर्पटी में)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Extrusive (volcanic) igneous rocks form when lava cools quickly at the surface, giving fine-grained rocks (e.g., basalt).

• "Plutonic" is named after Pluto, the Roman god of the underworld.

NOTE

• Igneous rocks are of two types: Intrusive/Plutonic (cooled inside — granite, gabbro) and Extrusive/Volcanic (cooled at the surface — basalt, obsidian).

question: Drains exiting from Mohenjo-Daro had _________ doors that were probably closed at night to prevent vagrants or negative elements from entering the city through that access.
solution_text:
The correct answer is wooden.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The drains exiting from Mohenjo-daro (a major site of the Harappan/Indus Valley Civilization) had "wooden" doors/gates that could be closed at night to prevent unwanted persons from entering the city through the drainage openings. (लकड़ी के दरवाज़े)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mohenjo-daro ("Mound of the Dead") was known for its advanced, covered drainage system, town planning on a grid, the Great Bath and the Great Granary.

• It was excavated by R. D. Banerji (1922) and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• The Harappan drainage system is considered one of the finest examples of ancient urban planning, with covered drains, manholes and soak pits.
